Forsyth wrote a book The Myth of Open Spaces in the context of Australia. Fiona Hill and Clifford Gaddy likewise demonstrated how population tends to concentrate, especially now with urbanization, using Russia as an example where migration is actually occurring from Siberia to European Russia. 

Already Siberia is empty and most Russians live west of the Urals, but the proportion is growing. Grover Clark in A Place in the Sun discussed how European governments were deluding themselves about acquiring colonies for excess population. Almost all European emigration was going to the US and Argentina and none of it was going to the vast European colonial holdings in Africa and Asia. 

So Geoff is right. Population tends to be highly concentrated and vast space does not mean vast expansion. Even the US has vast empty land in the Mountain States. All of Western China is empty too. 

Canada could probably better utilize her space but most of her territory is effectively useless. I think Gaddy and Hill would argue more strongly for the cold as a factor, and riverine communications.
